_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: Musa climbed the mountain for forty nights and came down with tablets of guidance for his people. But while he was gone, they had made a golden calf. Watch how God's book was received.
intro.curious: Musa, known in the Bible as Moses, climbed the mountain for forty nights and came down with tablets of guidance. But while he was gone, his people had made a golden calf. Watch what happened.

muslim.situation: You've decided to read the Quran every day, but it's been a week and you've skipped most days. A friend shares a funny video instead.

options.label: Watch videos and give up on the reading: it's not for you.
options.feedback: Musa's people turned to something shiny while guidance was on its way. Let's see what God says about His books.

options.label: Read one page with its meaning before anything else each day.
options.feedback: Small and steady. God sent His books to be lived with, not just owned.

options.label: Decide to read a lot on the weekend to make up for it.
options.feedback: Better than nothing, but a little every day lasts longer.

options.label: Keep the Quran on the shelf where people can see it.
options.feedback: A book on a shelf guides no one. The teaching explains what the books are for.

curious.situation: You've decided to read something meaningful every day, but after a week you've skipped most days. A friend sends you a funny video instead.

options.label: Watch the video and drop the reading.
options.feedback: It's easy to choose the shiny thing. See what Muslims believe God's books are for.

options.label: Read one page before anything else each day.
options.feedback: Small and steady: that's how Muslims are taught to keep company with scripture.

options.label: Catch up with a big read at the weekend.
options.feedback: Better than nothing, though a little each day tends to last.

options.label: Keep the book where people can see it.
options.feedback: A book on a shelf guides no one. The next step explains what scripture is for.

heading.muslim: What God teaches about His books
heading.curious: What Islam teaches about the revealed books

quran.about: God wrote for Musa on the tablets guidance and an explanation of everything, and told him to hold to it firmly.
God sent revelation to Nuh and the prophets after him, and gave Dawud the Psalms.
God gave Isa the Gospel, with guidance and light, confirming the Torah before it.
God sent down the Quran with the truth, confirming the scriptures before it and watching over them.
God sent down the Reminder, and He will guard it.

hadith.about: Belief in God's books is one of the six pillars of faith.
All the prophets brought one religion.

insights.text: Muslims believe in every book God revealed: the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa (87:18-19), the Torah of Musa, the Psalms of Dawud, the Gospel of Isa, and the Quran sent to Muhammad ﷺ, the last of them, which God promised to preserve (15:9).
The books were sent to be followed. Musa was told to hold the tablets firmly (7:145): guidance is something you take hold of, not just keep.

check.q: What did Musa bring down from the mountain?
check.why: He was given the tablets, written with guidance for his people (7:145).

check.q: What had the people done while Musa was away?
options: Made a golden calf and worshipped it
check.why: The Samiri cast a calf from their gold, and many worshipped it.

check.q: Which book was given to Dawud?
What does 15:9 promise about the Quran?
check.why: God sent down the Reminder and will guard it (15:9).

check.q: How does 5:48 describe the Quran's relation to earlier scriptures?
options: It confirms them and watches over them
It has nothing to do with them
check.why: The Quran confirms what came before and stands guard over it (5:48).

reflection.muslim: Which verse of the Quran has stayed with you most? Read it again today, slowly, with its meaning.
reflection.curious: Is there a book that has shaped how you live? What made it more than words on a page?
